metadata.topic: Rates of Reaction — Mass of H₂O₂ from Concentration
metadata.note: 1m: calculate mass of H₂O₂ given c=0.40 mol/dm³, V=1 dm³, M(H₂O₂)=34.01 g/mol. mass = c × V × M = 0.40 × 1 × 34.01 = 13.6g ±2%. Depends on Q1eii graph-read concentration (~0.40 mol/dm³). Own-figure answer accepted.

question.name: CSEC Chem May 2023 Q1f — Mass of H₂O₂ at Given Concentration
question.text:
The concentration of hydrogen peroxide at which the rate of reaction equals 0.045 s⁻¹ was determined from the graph to be approximately 0.40 mol dm⁻³.

Calculate the mass of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) dissolved in 1 dm³ of solution at this concentration.

[M(H₂O₂) = 34.01 g mol⁻¹] (1 mark)
question.general_feedback:
Calculating mass from concentration:

Formula: mass = concentration × volume × molar mass

mass = c × V × M

mass = 0.40 mol dm⁻³ × 1 dm³ × 34.01 g mol⁻¹

mass = 0.40 × 34.01 = 13.6 g

Derivation: n = c × V = 0.40 × 1 = 0.40 mol; mass = n × M = 0.40 × 34.01 = 13.6 g

Molar mass check: H₂O₂: (2 × 1) + (2 × 16) = 2 + 32 = 34 g mol⁻¹ ✓

steps.label:
Given: c = 0.40 mol dm⁻³ | V = 1 dm³ | M(H₂O₂) = 34.01 g mol⁻¹
Formula: mass = c × V × M (or: n = cV, then mass = nM)
Calculate the mass of H₂O₂. (1 mark)

fields.label: Mass of H₂O₂ = _____ g
fields.diagnostic_hint: mass = c × V × M = 0.40 × 1 × 34.01 = 13.6 g. Own-figure: if your concentration from the graph differs, apply the same formula with your value.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: mass = n × M = (c × V) × M = (0.40 × 1) × 34.01 = 0.40 × 34.01 = 13.6 g. Accept own-figure (your graph concentration × 34.01 g/mol).
